I read this as a read-only drag/drop geometry and split-composition diagnosis - I inspected the screenshot and design system, traced source/target payloads through the reducer and renderer, and ran the focused tests without editing files.

## Diagnosis

### Primary finding

The screenshot does **not** show a free-floating coordinate error.

The highlighted `New split` rectangle exactly matches the terminal group’s configured **top-edge hit target**:

- Terminal group body: approximately `x=292..813`, width `522px`
- Top zone CSS: 20% left/right inset and 20% height
- Expected geometry:
  - left: `292 + 522 × .20 = 396.4`
  - right: `813 - 522 × .20 = 708.6`
  - width: `313.2px`
  - body height approximately `818px`; 20% is `163.6px`
- Screenshot rectangle: approximately `x=396..709`, `y=70..233`

That is an exact match for:

```tsx
left-[20%] right-[20%] top-0 h-[20%]
```

at `ui/src/components/tab-dnd/TabGroupDropSurface.tsx:52`.

The apparent misalignment comes from two separate visuals:

1. `DragOverlay` follows the pointer and displays `main (2)`.
2. The edge target is parent-relative and highlights a 20%-deep hit region.

The edge region is **not a preview of the resulting 50/50 split**. The reducer creates a split with default ratio `0.5`, while the indicator displays only 20% of the target height. That semantic mismatch can make the preview look wrongly sized even though its coordinates are correct.

### Rendered composition finding

The existing terminal/browser layout appears to be:

```text
horizontal root
├── terminal tab group: main, main (2)
└── browser tab group: Browser
```

Dropping `main (2)` on the terminal group’s top edge does not split the entire root. It replaces only the targeted terminal group leaf:

```text
horizontal root
├── vertical nested split
│   ├── new group: main (2)
│   └── existing group: main
└── browser group: Browser
```

Therefore, the browser remaining independently rendered across the full right-hand side is expected from the current reducer semantics. This is the strongest explanation for the screenshot’s composition.

There is no terminal-versus-browser branch in the whole-tab split reducer. Both tab kinds take the same group-tree path; only the targeted group node determines where nesting occurs.

## File:line event trace

### 1. Drag source: `SortableTab`

`ui/src/components/tab-dnd/SortableTab.tsx:44-51`

```tsx
data: {
  type: "tab",
  tabId: tab.id,
  groupId,
  index,
}
id: `tab:${tab.id}`
```

The DOM mirrors the source identity at `SortableTab.tsx:72-75`:

- `data-tab-dnd-id`
- `data-tab-group-id`
- `data-tab-index`
- `data-dnd-type="tab"`

Both terminal and browser tabs use this same component and payload.

### 2. Actual screenshot target: group edge

Despite the presence of `SplitEdgeDropZone.tsx`, the currently rendered group zones are a separate private implementation.

`ui/src/components/tab-dnd/TabGroupDropSurface.tsx:12-29`

- Registers body ID: `group-body:${groupId}`
- Renders four group-edge zones.

`ui/src/components/tab-dnd/TabGroupDropSurface.tsx:34-38`

```tsx
id: `group-edge:${groupId}:${edge}`
data: { type: "group-edge", groupId, edge }
```

`ui/src/components/tab-dnd/TabGroupDropSurface.tsx:48-60`

- Parent-relative absolute geometry.
- Top target is centered 60% width and 20% height.
- `New split` feedback is rendered inside the zone.

The screenshot’s target is this private `TabGroupEdgeDropZone`, not `SplitEdgeDropZone`, because only the former is mounted by `TabGroupDropSurface`.

### 3. `SplitEdgeDropZone` and pane targets

`ui/src/components/tab-dnd/SplitEdgeDropZone.tsx:23-32`

Registers arbitrary edge IDs and data using `useDroppable`.

`ui/src/components/tab-dnd/SplitEdgeDropZone.tsx:63-72`

Defines the same 20% edge geometry.

`ui/src/components/tab-dnd/PaneEdgeDropZones.tsx:11-23`

Would register:

```text
pane-edge:${tabId}:${leafId}:${edge}
```

with:

```tsx
{ type: "pane-edge", tabId, leafId, edge }
```

However, `PaneEdgeDropZones` is not imported or rendered by `TerminalSplitView`. `PaneLeafView` currently registers only a whole-leaf target:

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.tsx:729-736`

```tsx
id: `pane-leaf:${tab.id}:${leafId}`
data: { type: "pane-leaf", tabId: tab.id, leafId }

id: `pane:${tab.id}:${leafId}`
data: { type: "pane", tabId: tab.id, leafId }
```

So pane-local edge geometry cannot explain the screenshot: it is not live in the current DOM.

### 4. Collision selection

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.tsx:55-74`

`workspaceCollisionDetection`:

1. Reads `active.data.current`.
2. Calls `pointerWithin`.
3. Maps collision IDs back to droppable data.
4. Rejects unsupported target types.
5. Sorts by `dropPriority`.

For tab drags, `ui/src/components/tab-dnd/tabDragTypes.ts:169-176` prioritizes:

1. Left/right group edge
2. Top/bottom group edge
3. Tab insertion
4. Group body

No coordinate conversion or viewport offset is done in application code; dnd-kit supplies pointer/rectangle collisions.

### 5. Drag-over preview

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.tsx:217-229`

For a `group-edge`, the preview activates the target group’s current active tab:

```tsx
groups[overData.groupId]?.activeTabId
```

This changes visible tab content during hovering but does not change target group IDs or tree geometry.

For a same-group drag like the screenshot, it ordinarily keeps the group’s existing active tab unless that is the dragged tab.

### 6. Drop command resolution

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.tsx:260-265`

`handleDragEnd` reads `event.over.data.current` and calls `executeDrop`.

`ui/src/components/tab-dnd/tabDragTypes.ts:102-118`

A tab over a group edge resolves to:

```tsx
{
  type: "move-tab-to-split",
  tabId: active.tabId,
  targetGroupId: over.groupId,
  direction,
  position,
}
```

`ui/src/components/tab-dnd/tabDragTypes.ts:184-189`

Top maps to:

```tsx
{ direction: "vertical", position: "first" }
```

### 7. Component callback to store action

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.tsx:248-250`

```tsx
onMoveTabToSplit(
  command.tabId,
  command.targetGroupId,
  command.direction,
  command.position,
)
```

`ui/src/App.tsx:804-807`

Passes the store’s `moveTabToSplit` directly into `TerminalSplitView`.

`ui/src/state/workspaceStore.ts:325-344`

Without a pane target, dispatches:

```tsx
{
  type: "MOVE_TAB_TO_SPLIT",
  sourceTabId,
  targetGroupId,
  direction,
  position,
}
```

`ui/src/state/workspaceStore.ts:944-949`

Delegates that action to `layoutReducer`.

### 8. Reducer tree mutation

`ui/src/state/layout.ts:315-363`

The reducer:

1. Finds the source tab and its source group.
2. Finds `groups[action.targetGroupId]`.
3. Removes the source tab from its old group.
4. Creates a new single-tab group.
5. Calls `splitTabGroupLeaf` with the exact target group ID.
6. Focuses the new group.

`ui/src/state/layout.ts:736-760`

`splitTabGroupLeaf` recursively finds only the matching group leaf and replaces it with:

```tsx
{
  type: "split",
  direction,
  first: position === "first" ? added : target,
  second: position === "first" ? target : added,
  ratio: 0.5,
}
```

It does not promote the split to the root. This is why targeting the terminal group leaves the browser sibling untouched.

### 9. Nested rendering

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.tsx:372-415`

`TabGroupLayoutRenderer` recursively renders every split node as a flex row or column.

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.tsx:383-391`

- Horizontal node → `flex-row`
- Vertical node → `flex-col`
- First child gets the stored percentage
- Second child gets remaining space

Thus a vertical split inserted beneath the terminal side of an existing horizontal terminal/browser root renders exactly as a nested split on the left.

### 10. Browser rendering distinction

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.tsx:578-604`

An active browser tab renders `BrowserPane`; a terminal tab renders `PaneRenderer`.

`ui/src/components/BrowserPane.tsx:24-47`

The browser body is a native child webview whose bounds are synchronized from the placeholder DOM rectangle.

`src-tauri/src/ipc/browser.rs:97-118`

Applies those logical bounds via `webview.set_bounds`.

This introduces a secondary integration risk: native child webviews are not ordinary DOM stacking content. CSS `z-index` cannot guarantee that a React drop indicator appears above the browser surface, and pointer movement over the child webview may not behave like movement over terminal DOM. The screenshot does not require this hypothesis—the browser correctly remains a separate sibling—but browser-edge drag behavior needs native integration coverage.

## Source/target ID assessment

For the currently working whole-tab/group path, there is no evidence of source or target ID corruption:

- Source data contains `tabId`, `groupId`, and `index`.
- Target data contains the exact target `groupId` and edge.
- No ID string parsing occurs after registration.
- Existing pointer resolver and store tests pass.
- Terminal and browser tabs share the same payload format.

The incomplete pane-edge path is different:

- `PaneEdgeDropData` is declared.
- `PaneEdgeDropZones` exists.
- The zones are not mounted.
- `isWorkspaceDropData` does not accept `"pane-edge"` at `tabDragTypes.ts:85-99`.
- `resolveWorkspaceDropCommand` does not handle `"pane-edge"`.
- `dropPriority` returns `100`, excluding it from collisions.
- Current pane drag data uses `leafId`, while the pane-handle runtime tests expect `sourcePaneId` and `sourceSessionId`.

Thus pane-edge events cannot currently reach any reducer action.

## Concrete hypotheses, ranked

1. **Confirmed: hit-target versus result-preview mismatch.**  
   The indicator is correctly positioned but represents a 20% hit target, while the resulting split is 50/50. This explains the undersized overlay.

2. **Confirmed: nested target-leaf rendering.**  
   A drop on the terminal group splits only that group, not the existing terminal/browser root. This explains why the browser remains unchanged on the right.

3. **Rejected for the whole-tab screenshot: bad source/target IDs.**  
   The whole-tab IDs and payload path are coherent, and related tests pass.

4. **Confirmed incomplete implementation: pane-edge IDs/data.**  
   Pane-edge targets are declared but neither mounted nor recognized by collision/command resolution.

5. **Possible browser-specific integration issue.**  
   Native webview stacking and event routing could prevent indicators or collisions over the browser body. This requires a Tauri-level test; the screenshot alone does not demonstrate it.

## Exact RED tests

### Already present and RED: pane-local geometry

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.paneDrop.runtime.test.tsx:70-95`

Keep this test. It precisely requires four `pane-edge` descendants per terminal leaf and currently fails because zero are mounted.

Current failure:

```text
expected to have a length of 4 but got 0
```

### Already present and RED: pane-edge collision priority and command

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.paneDrop.runtime.test.tsx:97-130`

Keep this test. It requires pane edges to outrank overlapping group edges and resolve to a pane-targeted split.

Current failure:

```text
expected 100 to be less than 1
```

### Already present and RED: pane drag source payload

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.paneHandleDrop.runtime.test.tsx:143-170`

Keep this test after settling the canonical field names. It currently expects:

```tsx
{
  type: "pane",
  tabId: "tab-main",
  sourcePaneId: "leaf-a",
  sourceSessionId: "session-a",
}
```

while the component emits:

```tsx
{
  type: "pane",
  tabId: "tab-main",
  leafId: "leaf-a",
}
```

### Already present and RED: pane-edge execution

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.paneHandleDrop.runtime.test.tsx:172-216`

Requires a multi-pane source to detach the existing PTY and merge it into a target leaf.

`ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.paneHandleDrop.runtime.test.tsx:218-272`

Requires a one-pane tab to move directly into the target leaf rather than disabling its only handle.

Both currently fail before reducer execution.

### Add: screenshot-shaped whole-tab dispatch integration

Add to `TerminalSplitView.pointerDrag.test.tsx`:

```tsx
it("dispatches a terminal tab top-edge drop to the exact terminal group, not the browser sibling", () => {
  // Layout:
  // horizontal root:
  //   group-terminal: main, main (2)
  //   group-browser: Browser
  //
  // Drag main (2), over:
  // { type: "group-edge", groupId: "group-terminal", edge: "top" }

  expect(onMoveTabToSplit).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
    "tab-main-2",
    "group-terminal",
    "vertical",
    "first",
  );
});
```

Also assert that the registered target is:

```tsx
{
  id: "group-edge:group-terminal:top",
  data: {
    type: "group-edge",
    groupId: "group-terminal",
    edge: "top",
  },
}
```

This isolates IDs from geometry and reducer behavior.

### Add: final tree composition integration

Add to `workspaceStore.tabDrop.test.tsx` using a pre-existing horizontal terminal/browser root:

```tsx
it("nests a top split inside the targeted terminal group without restructuring the browser sibling", () => {
  // Start:
  // horizontal(group-terminal, group-browser)
  //
  // Move tab-main-2 to group-terminal/top.

  expect(layout.tabGroupLayout).toEqual({
    type: "split",
    direction: "horizontal",
    first: {
      type: "split",
      direction: "vertical",
      first: { type: "group", groupId: sourceGroupId },
      second: { type: "group", groupId: "group-terminal" },
      ratio: 0.5,
    },
    second: { type: "group", groupId: "group-browser" },
    ratio: 0.5,
  });
});
```

This is the exact characterization test for current reducer semantics.

If product intent is instead “top means split the entire workspace root,” invert the expectation:

```tsx
expect(layout.tabGroupLayout).toEqual({
  type: "split",
  direction: "vertical",
  first: { type: "group", groupId: sourceGroupId },
  second: originalHorizontalRoot,
  ratio: 0.5,
});
```

That version will be RED against the current implementation and directly captures the composition discrepancy.

### Add: renderer structure test

Add to `TerminalSplitView.test.tsx`:

```tsx
it("renders a nested terminal top split while preserving the browser group as the root horizontal sibling", () => {
  render(<TerminalSplitView layout={postDropLayout} ... />);

  const root = screen.getAllByTestId("tab-group-split")[0];
  expect(root).toHaveAttribute("data-direction", "horizontal");

  const terminalBranch = root.children[0];
  expect(
    terminalBranch.querySelector('[data-testid="tab-group-split"][data-direction="vertical"]'),
  ).toBeInTheDocument();

  expect(
    root.children[2].querySelector('[data-tab-group-panel-id="group-browser"]'),
  ).toBeInTheDocument();
  expect(
    root.children[2].querySelector('[data-testid="browser-viewport"]'),
  ).toBeInTheDocument();
});
```

This separates reducer correctness from renderer correctness.

### Add: geometry/result-preview contract test

The product must choose one contract.

If the visual is only a hit-target highlight, add a geometry contract around the existing classes:

```tsx
expect(topZone).toHaveClass(
  "left-[20%]",
  "right-[20%]",
  "top-0",
  "h-[20%]",
);
```

If it is intended as a final-layout preview, add the RED expectation:

```tsx
expect(topFeedback).toHaveClass("inset-x-0", "top-0", "h-1/2");
```

The latter fails today and would force separation between:

- invisible 20% collision target, and
- visible 50% split preview.

That separation is the cleanest testable fix for the screenshot’s perceived misalignment.

### Add: browser native bounds integration

Extend `BrowserPane.test.tsx` with a controllable `ResizeObserver`:

```tsx
it("updates native browser bounds after its tab-group rectangle changes", async () => {
  // Initial rect: x=815, y=109, width=520, height=778.
  // Trigger ResizeObserver after a group split changes the rect.
  // New rect: x=1075, y=109, width=260, height=778.

  expect(setBrowserBounds).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith("browser-1", {
    x: 1075,
    y: 109,
    width: 260,
    height: 778,
  });
});
```

A true native/Tauri integration test should additionally verify that dragging over the child webview can still produce `group-edge:group-browser:*` collisions or that the child webview is temporarily hidden during a workspace drag.

## Verification output

Command run:

```text
cd ui && bunx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 \
  src/components/tab-dnd/SplitEdgeDropZone.test.tsx \
  src/components/TerminalSplitView.pointerDrag.test.tsx \

  src/components/TerminalSplitView.tabDropFallback.test.tsx \
  src/components/TerminalSplitView.paneDrop.runtime.test.tsx \
  src/components/TerminalSplitView.paneHandleDrop.runtime.test.tsx \
  src/components/TabBar.test.tsx \
  src/state/workspaceStore.tabDrop.test.tsx \
  src/state/workspaceStore.paneDrop.runtime.test.tsx \
  src/state/layout.test.ts \
  src/state/layout.paneHandleDrop.runtime.test.ts \
  src/components/BrowserPane.test.tsx
```

Exact summary:

```text
Test Files  2 failed | 10 passed (12)
Tests       5 failed | 58 passed (63)
Duration    15.99s
```

Failures:

```text
TerminalSplitView.paneDrop.runtime.test.tsx
- registers four edge drop zones inside every rendered terminal pane
  expected length 4, received 0
- always resolves the hovered pane edge ahead of the overlapping group edge
  expected 100 to be less than 1

TerminalSplitView.paneHandleDrop.runtime.test.tsx
- pane toolbar source payload differs from expected pane/session payload
- detach + pane-targeted merge callback was never called
- one-pane source is disabled and uses the old payload
```

All focused whole-tab group split, browser tab movement, reducer, renderer, fallback, and shared feedback tests passed.

## Design-system observation

The UI has a coherent tokenized Tailwind system:

- Semantic color variables in `ui/src/index.css`
- Tailwind mappings and layout tokens in `ui/tailwind.config.js`
- Shared patterns across `BrowserPane`, `BrowserToolbar`, `TerminalPane`, `WorkspaceHeader`, `Sidebar`, `IconButton`, `StatusDot`, and `SectionHeader`

The drag feedback correctly uses semantic tokens such as `border-primary`, `bg-primary/20`, and `bg-background/80`. The geometry itself is duplicated as hardcoded `20%` classes in both `TabGroupDropSurface.tsx` and `SplitEdgeDropZone.tsx`, which allows the live group target and the unfinished shared target implementation to diverge.

No files were edited.
